requirement.evidence: The Santa Ana City Council has adopted a new ordinance to strengthen renter protections by limiting the use of certain rent-setting software for residential properties.
requirement.note: The document also says the ordinance bans certain tools, lets tenants sue, and requires only proof that the software was used, not collusion. The nonpublic-data description comes from the document's explanation of the concern, so it is a reasonable reading.

key_value.evidence: Impacted tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney’s fees.

status.evidence: The Santa Ana City Council has adopted a new ordinance to strengthen renter protections by limiting the use of certain rent-setting software for residential properties.
status.note: The document presents the ordinance as adopted and current law. It gives no effective date or any sign that it was repealed.

citation.evidence: Approved on March 3, 2026, this action responds to concerns that some tools use nonpublic market data—such as real-time rents, lease activity, and occupancy levels—to influence pricing in ways that may drive rents higher.
citation.note: The adoption date matches. The document gives no ordinance number, as the card itself notes.
